frequency_question: What proportion of extreme regulatory fee spikes proposed by executive agencies successfully reach final rule publication without permanent judicial injunction or withdrawal before the end of the presidential term window?
membership_rule: Includes major fee adjustments exceeding 300% of baseline costs pursued via federal rulemaking in employment-based immigration, labor, or transportation sectors. Excludes minor inflation adjustments or non-fee regulatory changes.

cases.name: USCIS Comprehensive Fee Rule of 2020 (Hike up to 500% for certain categories)
EB-5 Immigrant Investor Program Modernization Rule (85% increase)
DHS Asylum Application Fee and Processing Fee Rule

coverage_note: 3 named; represents the universe of extreme fee-hike rulemakings of this magnitude in recent decades.
known_gaps: Extremely rare to see a fee increase as high as $103,265 proposed, making direct historical matches sparse.
skeleton: Three major high-stakes administrative fee rulemaking cycles attempted by DHS/USCIS in periods of intense political and economic scrutiny, yielding 1 successful final rule implementation out of 3 major attempts.
validity_reason: Base rate tied to the current administrative policy environment and judicial review standards, which remain constant through the current presidential term.
